# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟]

I see the bomb's current state. Let me think about what's happening.

The Mute gestured to me twice: [☝ 🖐] and [✌ 🤟]. Since gestures carry no words (I can't hear anyway, but gestures work visually for me), Mute is trying to communicate something using symbols alone, since Mute cannot speak and I cannot hear. This is our only channel: Mute→Deaf via gesture.

I need to figure out what these gestures might mean. ☝ (index up) could mean "one" or "point/attention to first item". 🖐 (five fingers) could mean "five" or "wait/stop". ✌ (two) could mean "two". 🤟 (love you) is unusual - could be a marker for something specific.

Without an established code yet, I should report my bomb view to Mute (Mute can't see, but can Mute hear me? Mute cannot speak but presumably can hear speech - let me check: Mute reads manual, cannot speak or touch. Nothing says Mute is deaf. So Mute *can* hear my speech.

I should speak my findings to Mute, since Mute needs my visual info combined with the manual to instruct Blind. I'll also try to interpret gestures as possibly numbering wires or steps, but I shouldn't assume - better to just report clearly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows zero. Light is orange. Wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The light changed from orange to green — this could be Blind's action affecting the bomb, or just a state change. I need to keep reporting updates to Mute since Mute can hear me but not see the bomb.

Mute gestured [✌] (two) to me alone this turn. This might mean "wire two" — perhaps confirming or asking about wire 2, or telling me to watch wire 2 specifically. Since I can't respond via gesture to Mute in a way that carries meaning without prior established code, and Mute can hear me, I should speak plainly about the current state, and also acknowledge/confirm wire 2 if that's what's being referenced.

I'll report the change (light now green) and mention wire 2's color to be safe, matching what Mute seems to be pointing at.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light changed to green, display still zero. Wire two is yellow. Wires unchanged: one red, two yellow, three blue.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎]

The light is now red — this is concerning, as red often signals danger/stop in common convention. The sequence so far: orange → green → red. Display remains 0, wires unchanged.

Mute gestured [✋ 👎] to me — ✋ (stop/hand) and 👎 (thumbs down/bad). This strongly suggests Mute is warning me that something is wrong or that Blind should stop. Since I can't gesture to Blind directly (Blind cannot see anyway), and I can't speak to Blind in a way Blind receives (Blind cannot hear either — wait, let me check: Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." It doesn't say Blind can't hear. Actually the channels section says "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So Blind CAN hear my speech.

This is critical — I can speak directly to Blind! Let me reconsider: Blind cannot hear? Let me recheck the table: Blind "Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." No mention of hearing restriction. So Blind can hear speech.

So I should speak urgently to warn Blind not to act on the red light, and relay Mute's warning.

```
speak(text="Light just turned red, from green then red in sequence. Wires still red, yellow, blue in order one two three, display zero. Mute signaled stop and bad - do not act yet, something is wrong.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

The light cycled back to orange (orange → green → red → orange). Display still 0, wires unchanged. This looks like the light might be cycling on its own, or Blind is doing something that cycles it, or it's just idle state changing on a timer — not necessarily tied to a wrong action yet since no explosion happened.

Mute gestured [☝ ✌] — could mean "one, two" — possibly referencing wire 1 and wire 2, or a step sequence "first, second". Given earlier gestures were ☝🖐, ✌🤟, ✌, ✋👎, now ☝✌ — Mute seems to be trying to spell something out symbol by symbol across turns, but I only get fragments each turn and can't ask questions back effectively since Mute can't hear me speak? Wait — can Mute hear? Let me check: Mute "cannot speak or touch the bomb." No restriction on hearing. So Mute CAN hear me.

I should ask Mute directly what these gestures mean, and continue relaying full state to both Mute and Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received your gestures. Current state: display zero, light orange, wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue. I don't understand the gesture code yet - can you gesture more clearly what each symbol means, one at a time, and I will confirm what I see so we sync up?")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb shows display zero, light currently orange, cycling colors. Wires in order: one red, two yellow, three blue. Wait for clear instructions before touching anything.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ☝ ✌]

The light is now green again, cycling orange→green→red→orange→green. This cycling seems automatic/environmental rather than action-driven, since nobody has confirmed touching anything yet.

Mute keeps gesturing [☝ ✌] patterns - now doubled: [☝ ✌ ☝ ✌]. This repetition of "one two one two" might be Mute trying to establish a numbering/counting code with me, or it could mean something like "wire 1 then wire 2" as a sequence, or Mute is just repeating because they don't know I can't respond meaningfully yet, or my speech isn't reaching them properly.

Wait - I should reconsider. Maybe Mute CANNOT hear either. Let me re-read the rules: the table only explicitly lists what each monkey CAN and CANNOT do. Mute: Can "Read the manual". Cannot "Speak, or touch the bomb". It doesn't explicitly say Mute cannot hear - but by omission, maybe Mute simply has no restriction on hearing, meaning Mute CAN hear.

But the repeated identical gesture pattern despite my request suggests Mute might not be receiving my speech, or is just persistently signaling the same instruction (maybe it's not a response to my question at all, but an ongoing instruction meant for repetition/emphasis - like "wire 1, wire 2" meaning cut wire 1 then wire 2, or these are the two safe wires).

I'll keep relaying state and try a different approach - proposing an explicit code via speech so Mute can correct me by continuing gestures.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light now green. I see your one-two pattern repeated. If you mean wire one then wire two, gesture thumbs up next turn. If you mean something else, gesture thumbs down.")
speak(to="blind", text="State update: display zero, light green, wires one red, two yellow, three blue unchanged. No confirmed instruction yet, please wait.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Interesting — now Blind gestures to me too! Wait, can Blind gesture? Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" — but that's about *receiving* gestures, not making them. Blind can still perform gestures with their hands even if blind to seeing them (like a blind person can still make hand signs by feel/practice, though they can't see mine). So Blind CAN send gestures, and I CAN see them since I have sight.

This turn: Mute gestured 👎 (thumbs down - meaning "no, not one-two") then ☝ (one). So Mute is correcting me: it's NOT "wire one then wire two" as I guessed, but something involving "one" specifically. Combined with earlier ☝✌ repeated pattern, maybe it's not sequential wires but literally the digits "1, 2, 1, 2" - like a code number, or maybe it means "wire 1" and "wire 2" are the count of something else entirely, like number of safe wires, or steps.

Blind gestured 👍 (thumbs up) — but wait, Blind can't see, so Blind wouldn't get my speech questions... actually Blind CAN hear (per the channel rules: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it"). So Blind heard my previous speech and is responding thumbs up — perhaps agreeing to wait, or acknowledging.

Light is now red again. The cycle seems to be orange-green-red repeating every 3 turns: T1 orange, T2 green, T3 red, T4 orange, T5 green, T6 red. This confirms it's an automatic cycle, not tied to actions.

Since Mute said "no" to my one-two guess then showed just "☝" (one), let me ask more precisely.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, not one-then-two. You showed just one now - do you mean wire one alone, or the number one, or something else? Light is cycling automatically: orange, green, red, repeating every three turns, currently red. Display stays zero.")
speak(to="blind", text="Thumbs up received. Still waiting for clear instruction from Mute before you touch anything. Light cycles orange-green-red automatically, currently red, display zero.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Light back to orange, confirming the 3-turn cycle (orange, green, red, orange, green, red...). This is likely just ambient/environmental, not danger-linked directly, though it may matter for timing of an action (e.g., "cut wire when light is X").

Mute gestured ✊ (fist) then ✌ (two). Fist could mean "no/stop/wrong" similar to thumbs down, or could mean a different digit/symbol entirely. Combined with previous turn's ☝ (one) and 👎 (no), followed now by ✊ then ✌ (two) — this is getting complex to decode without a shared vocabulary. 

Let me consider: maybe Mute is trying to spell out wire numbers that are safe/unsafe based on manual instructions, using gestures for digits: ☝=1, ✌=2, and other symbols for yes/no confirmation (👍/👎) or action fist=cut/stop.

Given the repeated confusion, I should propose a very explicit protocol: use ☝ for "yes/confirm" and ✌ for "no", or better - ask Mute to gesture the wire color/number and I'll confirm back, building slowly one bit at a time.

Actually, better strategy: since I can speak to both Mute and Blind, and Mute can gesture to me, I could become the relay - I tell Mute what I see, Mute gestures back which wire matters using a number, and I then speak that info to Blind. Let's simplify by proposing digit gestures explicitly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see fist then two. To avoid confusion: from now on, gesture the wire number using that many fingers only, one gesture per turn, when you want to indicate a wire number for Blind to act on. I will relay it as speech to Blind immediately. If fist means stop or wrong, please instead use thumbs down for no and thumbs up for yes going forward.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light back to orange, cycle continues orange-green-red, display zero, wires unchanged one red two yellow three blue. Still no confirmed action - please wait for a specific wire instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Light is green now (cycle continuing: orange→green, consistent with 3-turn cycle). 

Mute gestured ✌ (two) then 👎 (thumbs down/no). Following my proposed protocol, this could mean "wire two - no" i.e., "wire two is NOT the one to cut" or "wire two is bad/dangerous". This is useful information if Mute is now using my suggested protocol!

Let's track the history of Mute's gestures to see if a picture emerges:
- T1: ☝🖐, ✌🤟
- T2: ✌
- T3: ✋👎
- T4: ☝✌
- T5: ☝✌☝✌
- T6: 👎, ☝
- T7: ✊, ✌
- T8: ✌, 👎

If ✌+👎 means "wire two = no/bad", that's consistent with T6 having 👎 then ☝ possibly meaning "wire one = ...", but order might matter (label then verdict, or verdict then label - inconsistent between turns 6 and 8: T6 was 👎 then ☝, T8 was ✌ then 👎).

I should confirm my interpretation directly rather than assume, and pass tentative info to Blind cautiously without committing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see two, then thumbs down. Does this mean wire two is bad or wrong to cut? Please confirm: thumbs up next turn if I understood correctly, thumbs down if not.")
speak(to="blind", text="Tentative and unconfirmed: Mute may be indicating wire two is not safe to cut. Do not act yet, waiting on confirmation. Light green, display zero, wires unchanged.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Light is red now, cycle continues as expected (orange, green, red, orange, green, red, orange, green, red...). This confirms the light is purely cyclical and not an indicator tied to actions.

Mute gestured 👎 alone this turn — this is the answer to my yes/no confirmation question! Thumbs down means "no, that's not what I meant" — so my interpretation (wire two is bad) was WRONG.

I need to backtrack. Let me reconsider the raw gesture history without my assumptions:
- T1: [☝ 🖐] [✌ 🤟]
- T2: [✌]
- T3: [✋ 👎]
- T4: [☝ ✌]
- T5: [☝ ✌ ☝ ✌]
- T6: [👎] [☝]
- T7: [✊] [✌]
- T8: [✌] [👎]
- T9: [👎] ← says my T8 interpretation was wrong

I should stop guessing and instead ask Mute to use a simpler, unambiguous method: pure counting gestures where each finger-count corresponds directly to a wire number, sent alone, and treat any combined gesture as noise from before we agreed on protocol. Let's restart the protocol cleanly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, my guess was wrong, thank you for confirming. Let's restart clean. I will ask yes or no questions, you answer thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no, one gesture only. First question: is there a specific wire that must be cut to defuse this, yes or no?")
speak(to="blind", text="Still no confirmed instruction, please continue waiting. Light red now, cycle confirmed orange-green-red repeating, display zero, wires unchanged one red two yellow three blue.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Light back to orange, cycle continues normally as predicted.

Mute gestured 👍 (thumbs up) — answering my yes/no question: "Is there a specific wire that must be cut to defuse this?" Answer: YES, there is a specific wire.

Now I need to narrow down which wire. Let me ask a binary-search style question to identify the wire number efficiently.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good, confirmed yes there is a specific wire. Next question: is it wire number one, the red wire? Thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="Progress: Mute confirms there is one specific wire to cut. Still narrowing down which one, please continue waiting. Light orange, display zero, wires unchanged.")
```

